planting.note: Direct sow after last frost in warm, fertile soil in full sun, spacing plants about 24 inches apart; the compact, semi-dwarf vines need less room than standard slicing cucumbers but still benefit from a short trellis or support.

directions: Fanfare is a 1994 All-America Selections winner valued for its unusually compact, semi-dwarf vine habit combined with full-sized, high-quality slicing cucumbers. Fruits are straight, cylindrical, and slightly tapered at the blossom end, reaching about 8-9 inches with crisp, flavorful, less-bitter flesh. The monoecious flowering habit (producing both male and female flowers) supports strong, extended fruit set and good disease tolerance. Its small plant footprint makes it a good option for gardeners with limited space who still want a classic full-size slicer.

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost into warm soil in full sun; provide a trellis for straight fruit and good air circulation; works well in high tunnels or protected culture as well as the open garden.

directions: Socrates is an organic, gynoecious, parthenocarpic Beit Alpha-type cucumber that sets seedless fruit without pollination, making it reliably productive even where pollinator activity is inconsistent. The dark green, thin-skinned fruits grow 7-8 inches long with tender, sweet, non-bitter flesh that needs no peeling. Bred for cooler growing conditions and protected culture, it also performs well in open garden plantings during the warm season. Harvest regularly at 7-8 inches for the best texture and flavor.

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost in warm, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; train vigorous vines up a trellis to save space and keep fruit clean and straight.

directions: Marketer is a 1943 All-America Selections winning slicing cucumber prized for its slender, smooth, dark green fruit with white spines, typically 8-9 inches long, and its sweet, mild flavor. The vigorous, heat-tolerant vines are highly productive over a long harvest season, performing well even in hot, humid conditions that stress newer hybrids. Though largely superseded in commercial production by disease-resistant modern hybrids, it remains a reliable, long-cropping choice for home gardeners wanting an old-fashioned slicer. Pick at 8-9 inches for the best fresh-eating quality.

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost in warm, fertile soil in full sun; train the vigorous vines onto a trellis to encourage long, straight fruit.

directions: Shintokiwa is a Japanese heirloom cucumber brought into American cultivation through biodynamic seed growers and producing long, slender, smooth-skinned fruit 9-12 inches long. The thin, tender skin and dense, nearly seedless flesh give it a crisp, sweet flavor with virtually no bitterness, making peeling unnecessary. Plants are vigorous and productive, with good resistance to bacterial wilt. Excellent for fresh eating and light pickling, and well suited to trellising for long, straight fruit.

common_name: Katrina Cucumber (Mini Beit Alpha Snacking Cucumber)

planting.note: Direct sow or transplant after last frost into warm soil in full sun; a trellis or support helps keep the smooth mini fruits clean and easy to harvest; well suited to high tunnels and hydroponic systems as well as open ground.

directions: Katrina is a hybrid Beit Alpha-type mini cucumber bred for snacking, bearing smooth, thin-skinned, nearly seedless fruit about 5.5-6.5 inches long with a sweet, crisp bite. It is heat-tolerant and highly productive, often setting multiple fruits per node for a heavy, early-to-midseason harvest. The seedless, parthenocarpic fruit set makes production reliable in both open gardens and protected culture. Harvest young and often at full size for the sweetest, crunchiest cucumbers with no need to peel.

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost in warm, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; pick frequently to keep vigorous vines productive through the season.

directions: A and C Pickling is a 1928 open-pollinated heirloom pickling cucumber bred by the Abbott and Cobb seed house of Philadelphia, producing heavy yields of dark green, blocky fruit 8-10 inches long at full size. The dark color holds well after harvest, an important trait for market growers and picklers alike. Pick at 4-6 inches for classic dill or gherkin-style pickles, or let a few size up for fresh eating. Vigorous, productive vines continue setting fruit over a long summer harvest with regular picking.
